details:
hear me out.

i think the decision to completely remove VP avatars from standalone was an alright idea for optimisation, but ultimately causes more harm than good for many people.

i typically like to use/make avatars that are in that "non problematic very poor 5%" that the performance rankings outline. the most fun avatars for me to make are those that are physically larger than usual; avatars that are larger in physical scale that go past the bounding box 5m x 6m x 5m limit, but being optimised in every other way, causing no real performance hit. 

these avatars were perfectly fine before the update, and quest friends reported no performance hit around these avatars, despite being very poor rated.

a direct quote from the performance ranks page, "there are many ways to have a well-optimized avatar appear as Very Poor, and have a FPS hog rank as Excellent." as this is the case, i think users should still get the option to manually enable very poor avatars.

i know this was a step taken for performance, so i propose a compromise, as i do agree, the older system was an issue for creators not optimising avatars.

a maximum amount of very poors loaded.

intentionally low, perhaps 2 or 3, so that those avatars that pass the "5%" litmus test for problematics.

this allows for flashier avatars to be still used in very small groups, or for avatars with one or two categories broken to be usable.

as someone who is a fan of titans, giants, all those kind of avatars, it hurts to have them just removed for the (unfortunately) most prominant part of the playerbase.
title: Re-add Very poor avatars to Standalone, with a compromise.
